messages:
anna_infra: Quick signal — we saw a cluster-wide bump in 429s across eu-west yesterday ~17:20 UTC when a couple of new jobs landed. Noticed SDK clients are hammering retries which amplified the pressure. paste of one response headers we captured:
```
status: 429
retry-after-ms: 12000
x-rw-admission: throttle
server-node: gpu-pool-11
```
Can infra/runtime team confirm the intended semantics for 429 vs 503 and any headers SDKs should rely on?

michael_sdk: Short answer: SDK currently treats any 429 as retryable with exponential backoff + jitter, max 4 retries. If Retry-After present we wait that long. But we don't surface admission reason to callers. Thinking we should parse one or two additional headers and expose them in exceptions/telemetry.

dinesh_runtime: From runtime side: we emit 429 when admission control rejects requests due to queue or token shortage (intentional backpressure). 503 is used when the node is unhealthy or network downstream failed. We can add clearer hints. Proposal: canonicalize headers: `Retry-After` (seconds OR ms fallback), `X-RW-Admission` (values: throttle|overload|maintenance), `X-RW-Queue-Pos` (integer hint). 429 + X-RW-Admission=throttle => client should back off aggressively and avoid retries burst.

sarah_oncall: Is `Retry-After` always present when 429 is admission? We saw some 429s without it which confused SDKs. That was from preflight path that hasn't been updated.

dinesh_runtime: Not always right now — bug. We should guarantee either `Retry-After` or `Retry-After-Ms` in admission 429 responses. Will prioritize.

michael_sdk: Ok. SDK plan suggestion: 1) Prefer server-provided `Retry-After` (s) or `Retry-After-Ms`. 2) If X-RW-Admission=throttle, apply larger multiplier on base backoff and drop retries after 2 attempts for non-idempotent calls. 3) Use full jitter (Rand(0, base * 2^n)) and cap at 30s. 4) Surface structured error with fields: status, retry_after_ms, admission_reason, queue_pos. 5) Attach telemetry event for every 429 with those fields so infra can correlate.

elaine_prod: From product side, we need a consistent user-facing story: SDKs should surface when behavior is transient vs persistent so customers can implement graceful degradation (e.g., fall back to cached answer). Can we also return a numeric capacity-hint to allow client-side rate-smoothing?

dinesh_runtime: We can add `X-RW-Capacity-Hint: 0-100` representing estimated percent of spare global capacity for that plan/route. It's noisy but helpful for client-side pacing. Will prototype.

michael_sdk: Nice. Implementation note: don't let clients use capacity-hint as absolute quota. Use smoothing window, e.g., EWMA, and throttle request rate accordingly. Also add a per-route retry budget to avoid cross-route amplification (default 10 retries/min per API key).

sarah_oncall: Action items for oncall/infra: - dinesh to ensure Retry-After header is present on admission 429s and add capacity-hint prototype (ETA 48h). - michael to PR SDK changes to parse/emit new fields and add telemetry sampling. - anna to create a dashboard showing 429 spikes correlated with SDK retry events.

anna_infra: small add — include a lightweight header `X-RW-Drop` with value `true` when we intentionally drop (no retry). Helps SDK to short-circuit.

michael_sdk: Good idea. We'll treat `X-RW-Drop: true` as non-retryable.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime/429-headers-fix v1.2.3 rolled to eu-west in canary (10% traffic) at 2026-03-18T18:43:01Z :white_check_mark:

anna_infra: Thanks. Let's reconvene after canary metrics. For the thread: I'll file the infra ticket and the SDK issue, link both in the dashboard ticket. :thumbsup:
